title: Blue Pill 的引脚：哪个脚能干什么
summary: Blue Pill 的引脚长得一样，本事不一样：有的耐 5 V，有的只能给 3 mA，只有几个能读模拟电压。先把 5 V 送错一次，再挑对引脚。
concepts: 5 V tolerant (FT) 耐 5 V 引脚
ADC pins 模拟输入引脚
description: STM32F103 “Blue Pill” 的逻辑电平是 3.3 V。标 FT 的引脚（PA8–PA15、PB3、PB4、PB6–PB15）能直接收 5 V，其他引脚不行。PC13–PC15 最多 3 mA；板载 LED 接在 PC13 上，输出低才亮。模拟输入（ADC）只在 PA0–PA7、PB0、PB1。

cards.title: 把 5 V 送错一次
text: 把 **Blue Pill** 插上面包板，让它的 5V 脚给下方电源轨供电。
然后把 5 V **故意**送进一个不该送的引脚，看诊断怎么说；再挪一列，送进旁边的引脚。
两个引脚紧挨着，为什么一个报警、一个没事？

cards.title: 引脚长得一样，本事不一样
text: - **单击开发板**，引脚列表里每一行都有小标签：**FT**、**ADC**、**3 mA**。接线之前先看标签。
- **FT = 耐 5 V。** 普通引脚里有一只通往 3V3 的保护二极管。送进 5 V，它就导通，电流从 5 V 灌进 3V3。FT 引脚没有这一只，能直接收 5 V 信号：
![](fig:clamp)
- 板上能用的 FT 引脚是 PA8–PA12、PA15、PB3、PB4、PB6–PB15（PA13、PA14 也耐 5 V，但留给下载器）。PB5 夹在中间，偏偏不是。
- **PC13–PC15 是弱引脚**，最多 3 mA。板载 LED 就接在 PC13 上，电流流进引脚，所以输出低才亮：
- 代入数字：要是外面再接一颗配 220 Ω 的红灯，$I = \frac{3.3 - 1.8}{220 + 12 + 40} ≈ 0.0055$ A，也就是 5.5 mA——PC13 吃不消。
- **模拟输入（ADC）**只在 PA0–PA7、PB0、PB1 上。它把 0–3.3 V 的电压读成数字，5.7 会细讲。

cards.title: 点板载灯，读一个电压
text: - 先让 PC13 输出低，点亮板载 LED，看它用了多少电流。
- 再用两个 `10 kΩ` 把 5 V 分成一半左右，送进模拟输入 PA0。ADC 引脚**不耐 5 V**，所以 5 V 不能直接接上去。
- 先预测：5V 脚比 5 V 低一点（107 课量过），分压器的中点是多少？

cards.title: 带走
text: - **接线之前先看引脚标签**：同一排相邻的两个脚，本事可能完全不同。
- **5 V 信号只能进 FT 引脚**，而且只能当输入（或者开漏输出，5.6 会讲）。
- **PC13–PC15 最多 3 mA**，只适合灌一点点电流；板载 LED 已经用掉了 PC13 的大半。
- 真实电路里的坑：ADC 引脚都不耐 5 V。5 V 传感器的输出要先分压，就像你刚搭的那样。

caption.text: 普通引脚里的保护二极管：引脚上的 5 V 比 3V3 高，二极管导通，电流 I 灌进 3V3。FT 引脚没有这一只。

i18n.en: The clamp diode inside an ordinary pin: 5 V on the pin is above 3V3, the diode conducts and a current I flows into 3V3. An FT pin has no such diode.

caption.text: 板载 LED：3V3 → 510 Ω → LED → PC13。PC13 输出低时，下开关（约 40 Ω）合上，电流 I 流进引脚。

i18n.en: The onboard LED: 3V3 → 510 Ω → LED → PC13. When PC13 outputs LOW its low side (about 40 Ω) is on and a current I flows into the pin.

tests.name: 5 V 进 FT 引脚读高；PA0 的电压在 ADC 量程内；PC13 点亮板载 LED，电流在 3 mA 以内

measurements.ask: 万用表：PA0（分压器的中点）对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 两个一样的电阻把 5V 脚的电压平分。5V 脚约 4.68 V（USB 后面有一只二极管），所以中点约 2.34 V，在 0–3.3 V 的量程里。

measurements.ask: PC13 输出低、板载 LED 亮着：万用表测 PC13 对 GND 的电压
measurements.explain: 电流流过下开关的约 40 Ω：40 × 0.00265 ≈ 0.106 V。低电平也不是正好 0 V。

measurements.ask: 用你的读数算流进 PC13 的电流：I = V / 40 Ω

choices: 不行：板载 LED 已经用了约 2.7 mA，再加 1.4 mA 就超过 3 mA
可以：1 kΩ 的电流很小
可以：PC13 是普通引脚，能给 20 mA
measurements.ask: 想在 PC13 上再接一颗配 1 kΩ 的 LED（也是灌电流），行吗？
measurements.explain: 两颗灯的电流都流进 PC13：2.7 + (3.3 − 1.8) / (1000 + 12 + 40) ≈ 4.1 mA，超过了 3 mA。要多接灯，换一个普通引脚。

choices: PA0：它是 ADC，什么电压都能读
measurements.ask: 一个 5 V 供电的传感器输出 0 / 5 V 的数字信号，直接接 Blue Pill 的哪个引脚？
measurements.explain: 只有 FT 引脚能直接收 5 V。PB5 和 PA0 都不耐 5 V，5 V 会让保护二极管导通；要接它们，先分压。

steps.text: 选**「STM32 最小系统板 Blue Pill」**，单击 **`c1`**（左上角的 GND 脚）。上排针插在 c 行、下排插在 g 行，各占 20 列。USB 默认插着。
下方电源轨接上 5 V：红色跳线 **`j18`** → **`bp18`**（5V 脚），蓝色跳线 **`j19`** → **`bn19`**（GND 脚）。下方红轨现在是 5 V。
**故意接错一次**：黄色跳线 **`bp13`** → **`j13`**，把 5 V 直接送进 **PB5**。**单击开发板**，看 PB5 那一行和右边的**诊断**。
选中这根跳线，按 **Delete** 删掉。
挪一列再接：黄色跳线 **`bp14`** → **`j14`**，5 V 进 **PB6**。PB6 读到什么？诊断还报警吗？在引脚列表里比一比 PB5 和 PB6 的小标签。
**单击开发板**，把 **PC13** 设成**「输出 低」**。板子上的小灯亮了。看 PC13 那一行：电流是负的，表示电流流**进**引脚。
把 **PA0** 设成**「ADC」**（模拟输入）。引脚列表里会显示它读到的电压。
点**「检查我的电路」**，再用万用表和引脚列表回答测量题。

hints: 单击开发板，引脚列表里每一行的小标签说明这个脚能干什么：FT（耐 5 V）、ADC、3 mA（弱引脚）。
下排从左数：PB12、PB13、PB14、PB15、PA8……第 13 列是 PB5，第 14 列是 PB6，第 18 列是 5V，第 19 列是 GND。
上排第 16 列是 PA0，第 19 列是 PC13；空孔在 a、b 行。

en.title: Blue Pill pins: which pin does what
en.summary: The Blue Pill's pins look alike but can do different things: some take 5 V, some give only 3 mA, only a few read analog voltages. Send 5 V to the wrong pin once, then pick the right ones.
en.description: The STM32F103 "Blue Pill" runs at 3.3 V logic. Pins marked FT (PA8–PA15, PB3, PB4, PB6–PB15) can take 5 V directly; the others cannot. PC13–PC15 give at most 3 mA; the onboard LED is on PC13 and lights when the pin outputs LOW. Analog inputs (ADC) are only PA0–PA7, PB0 and PB1.

cards.title: Send 5 V to the wrong pin once
text: Plug the **Blue Pill** into the breadboard and let its 5V pin power the bottom rails.
Then send 5 V into a pin where it does not belong, **on purpose**, and see what the diagnostics say; then move one column over to the next pin.
The two pins sit side by side — why does one complain and the other not?

cards.title: Pins that look alike, but aren't
text: - **Click the board**: every row of the pin list has little tags — **FT**, **ADC**, **3 mA**. Read the tags before you wire.

- **FT = five-volt tolerant.** An ordinary pin has a clamp diode to 3V3 inside. Feed it 5 V and the diode conducts, pushing current from 5 V into 3V3. An FT pin has no such diode and can take a 5 V signal directly:
![](fig:clamp)
- The usable FT pins are PA8–PA12, PA15, PB3, PB4 and PB6–PB15 (PA13 and PA14 are FT too, but reserved for the programmer). PB5 sits in the middle and is the odd one out.
- **PC13–PC15 are weak pins**, 3 mA at most. The onboard LED hangs on PC13 with its current flowing into the pin, so it lights on LOW:
- With numbers: add one more red LED with 220 Ω outside, and $I = \frac{3.3 - 1.8}{220 + 12 + 40} ≈ 0.0055$ A, that is 5.5 mA — too much for PC13.
- **Analog inputs (ADC)** are only on PA0–PA7, PB0 and PB1. They turn a voltage of 0–3.3 V into a number; 5.7 goes into detail.

cards.title: Light the onboard LED, read a voltage
text: - First make PC13 output LOW to light the onboard LED, and see how much current it takes.
- Then split 5 V roughly in half with two `10 kΩ` and feed it to the analog input PA0. ADC pins are **not 5 V tolerant**, so 5 V cannot go there directly.
- Predict first: the 5V pin is a little under 5 V (you measured it in the dev-board lesson). What is the divider's midpoint?

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Read the pin tags before wiring**: two neighbouring pins in one row can do completely different things.
- **5 V signals only go into FT pins**, and only as inputs (or open-drain outputs, see 5.6).
- **PC13–PC15 give at most 3 mA** and are only good for sinking a little current; the onboard LED already uses most of PC13's share.
- A real-circuit catch: no ADC pin is 5 V tolerant. A 5 V sensor's output needs a divider first, just like the one you built.

steps: Pick **STM32 Blue Pill** and click **`c1`** (the GND pin at the top left). The upper pins go into row c and the lower pins into row g, 20 columns each. USB is plugged in by default.
Put 5 V on the bottom rails: red jumper **`j18`** → **`bp18`** (the 5V pin), blue jumper **`j19`** → **`bn19`** (a GND pin). The bottom red rail is now 5 V.
**Get it wrong on purpose**: yellow jumper **`bp13`** → **`j13`**, putting 5 V straight into **PB5**. **Click the board** and look at PB5's row and the **diagnostics** on the right.
One column over: yellow jumper **`bp14`** → **`j14`**, 5 V into **PB6**. What does PB6 read? Do the diagnostics still complain? Compare the little tags of PB5 and PB6 in the pin list.
**Click the board** and set **PC13** to **OUT LOW**. The little LED on the board lights. Look at PC13's row: the current is negative, meaning it flows **into** the pin.
A divider: two **`10 kΩ`** resistors. R1 from **`bp22`** to **`j22`**, R2 from **`i22`** to **`bn22`**. The lower half of column 22 now sits at about half of 5 V.
Jumper **`g22`** → **`a16`**: the divider's midpoint goes to **PA0**.
Set **PA0** to **ADC** (analog input). The pin list shows the voltage it reads.
Press **Check my circuit**, then answer the questions with the multimeter and the pin list.

measurements.ask: Multimeter: PA0 (the divider's midpoint) to GND
measurements.explain: Two equal resistors split the 5V pin's voltage in half. The 5V pin is about 4.68 V (there is a diode after USB), so the midpoint is about 2.34 V, inside the 0–3.3 V range.

measurements.ask: PC13 output LOW, onboard LED lit: multimeter on PC13 to GND
measurements.explain: The current flows through the low side's 40 Ω or so: 40 × 0.00265 ≈ 0.106 V. A LOW is not exactly 0 V.

measurements.ask: From your reading, the current into PC13: I = V / 40 Ω
measurements.explain: (3.3 − 1.8) / (510 + 12 + 40) ≈ 2.7 mA, just under the 3 mA limit.

measurements.ask: You want one more LED with 1 kΩ on PC13 (sinking too). Can you?
choices: No: the onboard LED already takes about 2.7 mA, and another 1.4 mA would pass 3 mA
Yes: PC13 is an ordinary pin that gives 20 mA
measurements.explain: Both LEDs' currents flow into PC13: 2.7 + (3.3 − 1.8) / (1000 + 12 + 40) ≈ 4.1 mA, over 3 mA. For more LEDs, use an ordinary pin.

measurements.ask: A 5 V sensor puts out a 0 / 5 V digital signal. Which Blue Pill pin can take it directly?
choices: PA0: it's an ADC pin, it reads any voltage
measurements.explain: Only FT pins take 5 V directly. PB5 and PA0 are not 5 V tolerant: 5 V turns their clamp diode on. To use them, divide the voltage first.

hints: Click the board: the tags on each row of the pin list say what the pin can do — FT (5 V tolerant), ADC, 3 mA (weak pin).
The lower row from the left: PB12, PB13, PB14, PB15, PA8 … column 13 is PB5, column 14 is PB6, column 18 is 5V, column 19 is GND.
In the upper row, column 16 is PA0 and column 19 is PC13; the free holes are in rows a and b.
tests: 5 V into an FT pin reads high; PA0 inside the ADC range; PC13 lights the onboard LED under 3 mA
